datasets.name: Tibetan Plateau landslide remote sensing image dataset
datasets.verbatim: a Tibetan Plateau landslide remote sensing image dataset is curated, consisting of landslides, rainfall-induced debris, and freeze–thaw-induced debris.

datasets.name: Google Earth imagery
datasets.verbatim: Leveraging the unique characteristics of the three types of geological hazard, additional corresponding landslides on the Tibetan Plateau are searched for on Google Earth. Google Earth, renowned for its spatial resolution of 0.14 m, serves as a widely utilized data source (Cheng et al. 2021).

datasets.name: Global landslide inventory (Froude and Petley 2018)
datasets.verbatim: To verify the accuracy of GLDM in identifying landslides, the data from Froude and Petley (2018) was used to test the model's performance.

methods.name: GLDM (Global Landslide Detection Model)
methods.summary: GLDM is a deep learning-based landslide detection model that improves the YOLOX architecture by incorporating ASFF (Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion) to handle large-scale data diversity and enhance feature scale consistency. It uses a backbone based on CSPDarknet53 and a decoupled head for classification and localization, trained on a curated Tibetan Plateau landslide dataset.
methods.verbatim: we propose a novel global landslide detection model (GLDM) that improves the YOLOX architecture to better handle large-scale data diversity and enhance model generalization.
